references.text: The Lord appears to Jacob at Bethel (Luz) and gives him promises of land and descendants. Jacob refers back to this event in Gen 48:3.
Jacob names the place Luz, Bethel, which clarifies the place reference 'Luz' in Gen 48:3.
God appears again to Jacob at Luz (Bethel) in the land of Canaan, blesses him, and confirms the promises. This is the event Jacob most directly refers to in 48:3.
God reveals himself to Abram as El Shaddai and gives him promises. This is the first use of the divine name 'El Shaddai', the same name Jacob uses in 48:3.
48:3 explicitly refers to the event described in 35:9; the two verses together form the memory and account of the same divine revelation.
Both verses confirm God's continuous faithfulness and presence in Jacob's life, from the first revelation at Luz to his final blessing.
Both verses document critical moments in Jacob's life where he experiences a direct encounter with God ('to see God'), which defines his identity and faith.
The verses form a theological arc where Jacob's vow at Bethel in 28:20 is confirmed and fulfilled through God's blessing that he recalls in 48:3.
